correctness.rationale: For each tree pair, path survival yields F_T(p)=sum_{j>=1} a_j(T) p^{j+1}. Equal n forces cancellation of p^2 and at p=1. An exhaustive leaf-attachment generator with center-root canonical encodings enumerates every unlabeled tree through order 11, groups exact distance vectors, and applies the exact integer Möbius transformation plus Descartes sign variations. There is one potential n=11 exception; its residual cubic 3p^3+p^2-3p+1 has discriminant -76 and only real root negative. The explicit n=12 edge lists yield exact distance vectors and F_A-F_B=p^3(p-1)(2p-1)(p^3+p^2-1), hence two simple positive interior roots. CHECK.py independently computes the complete finite part and all witness coefficients without external input. No extrapolation beyond n=12.

originality.rationale: Theorem is not the classical Wiener/Hosoya identity or the known bond-percolation pair-resilience model: it is the minimal *tree order* (12) permitting two strict positive-parameter intersections of two equal-order expected pair-connectivity curves. The full articles read by Keitt et al (landscape fragmentation), Saura et al (stepping-stone habitat networks), Mowshowitz and Dehmer (Hosoya entropy), and Brown et al (complex and real roots of individual Wiener polynomials; explicitly identifying edge-percolation pair resilience) do not claim or imply the sharp smallest-order two-difference-crossing threshold. Seven actual semantic database searches and compared published related results identified no covering theorem. This is evidence-based provisional priority, not proof of global novelty.
residual_risks: Historical priority has not been independently established; unindexed literature on ordering of Wiener/Hosoya polynomials or pair reliability might contain an equivalent crossing threshold.
A landscape graph need not be a tree and patch failures are rarely independent or homogeneous; no applied transfer without independent model checking.
The source date of Keitt et al is resolved only to year, not an exact earliest day; archival classification rests on the verified online 2013 source date.

value.rationale: Expected connected retained habitat-patch pairs is a natural, decision-interpretable functional connectivity statistic in tree-shaped fragmented landscapes, not a synthetic arbitrary invariant. The sharp minimal 12-site onset demonstrates the smallest scale at which rankings reverse twice as survival probability changes, a concrete limitation of one-parameter conservation ranking. The theorem is a natural exact finite cutoff, with caveats that its simplified ecological assumptions require separate validation.
